section_summary: This section contains Department of State and Department of the Army correspondence, applications, telegrams, and memoranda from late March to mid-April 1949 concerning travel clearances and military permits for entry into occupied Japan and Korea. It documents commercial representatives seeking entry for trade, property restitution, and government purchasing missions, as well as transit authorizations and procedures for individuals visiting relatives in Japan. Inquiries and clearances involve applicants from the United States, China, Egypt, Venezuela, Canada, Siam, and other nations, coordinated between the Division of Protective Services, the Department of Commerce, and the Pacific Military Permit Branch.
